title: Where Does the Puddle Go?
learning_objectives: Learn that water from a puddle goes into the air (evaporates) and into the ground
Use the word evaporate in context

factual_claims.claim: Some puddle water soaks down into the soil.
factual_claims.source: USGS Water Science School, 'Infiltration and the Water Cycle' (usgs.gov)

factual_claims.claim: Some puddle water turns into water vapor and goes into the air; this is called evaporation.
factual_claims.source: USGS Water Science School, 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle' (usgs.gov); NASA Climate Kids, 'What is the water cycle?'

factual_claims.claim: Water vapor is invisible; you cannot see it in the air.
factual_claims.source: USGS Water Science School, 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle' (water vapor is a gas, invisible)

factual_claims.claim: Warmth from the sun makes water evaporate faster.
factual_claims.source: NASA Climate Kids, 'What is the water cycle?' (heat from the sun causes evaporation); USGS, 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle'

factual_claims.claim: Water vapor in the air can form clouds and fall again as rain.
factual_claims.source: NASA Climate Kids, 'What is the water cycle?'

parent_prompts: After reading: Where did the puddle water go? Two places. Which one can we not see?

pages.text: After the rain, there is a puddle on the path.
pages.illustration_brief: A wide puddle on a dirt path reflecting grey sky; drips from a leaf.
pages.audio_script: After the rain, there is a puddle on the path.

vocabulary.definition: A small pool of rain water on the ground.

pages.text: The next day the puddle is smaller. Where did the water go?
pages.illustration_brief: Same path, a smaller puddle with a damp ring around it; sun out.
pages.audio_script: The next day the puddle is smaller. Where did the water go?

pages.text: Some water soaks down into the soil. The ground drinks it.
pages.illustration_brief: Cross-section: the puddle on top, blue arrows pointing down into brown soil.
pages.audio_script: Some water soaks down into the soil. The ground drinks it.

vocabulary.definition: Goes slowly into something, like water into a sponge.
vocabulary.example: The rain soaks into my socks.

pages.text: Some water goes up into the air. It turns into water vapor. You cannot see it.
pages.illustration_brief: The puddle with faint wavy arrows rising into empty air; nothing visible above.
pages.audio_script: Some water goes up into the air. It turns into water vapor. You cannot see it.

vocabulary.definition: Water that has turned into a gas and floats in the air.
vocabulary.example: Steam from a hot cup is water vapor you can just see.

pages.text: This is called evaporation. The warm sun makes it happen faster.
pages.illustration_brief: A bright sun over the shrinking puddle; more rising arrows on the sunny side.
pages.audio_script: This is called evaporation. The warm sun makes it happen faster.

vocabulary.definition: When water turns into vapor and goes into the air.
vocabulary.example: Wet clothes dry because of evaporation.

pages.text: Up high, the vapor can make clouds. One day it will fall as rain and make a new puddle.
pages.illustration_brief: A small cloud above the now-dry path; a single raindrop falling from it.
pages.audio_script: Up high, the vapor can make clouds. One day it will fall as rain and make a new puddle.

quiz.prompt: Where are the two places the puddle water goes?

options.text: Into the soil and into the air
Into a river and a lake

quiz.explanation: Page 3: some soaks into the soil. Page 4: some goes up into the air.

options.text: Water turning into vapor and going into the air

quiz.explanation: Page 4 explains water going into the air as vapor; page 5 names this evaporation.

quiz.prompt: What makes the puddle dry up faster?
quiz.explanation: Page 5 says: The warm sun makes it happen faster.

quiz.prompt: What is this book mostly about?
quiz.explanation: Page 2 asks where the water went. The rest of the book, up to page 6, answers it.

quiz.prompt: In your own words, tell a grown-up where puddle water goes. Try to use the word evaporation.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says it dries; with support: names the ground or the air with prompting; independent: soil and air, uses evaporation, mentions sun or clouds
quiz.explanation: A two-place explanation with the key word shows the concept was understood, not memorized.

activities.prompt: Put the water's journey in order.

items.text: Water soaks into the soil and evaporates into the air.
Rain falls and makes a new puddle.

activities.prompt: Match the word to its meaning.

pairs.right: a small pool of rain water

off_screen_prompt: Put a spoon of water on a plate in the sun and another in the shade. Check them after lunch. Which one went first?
